title: Claude Files Pane Shows Live File Tree for Code Edits
summary: New open-source Claude Files Pane extension visualizes Claude Code's file operations in real-time, tracking reads, writes, and agent activity.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Open-source Claude Files Pane extension now tracks Claude Code file operations in a live visual tree interface.
- The tool displays which files the AI agent reads, edits, or creates during coding sessions in real time.
- Developers gain transparency into Claude Code's workspace activity, improving debugging and oversight of agent behavior.


A new open-source browser extension called Claude Files Pane brings real-time file operation visibility to[Claude Code](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-code-review) users. Developed by Marius Adam and officially released on November 1, 2026, the tool displays a live file tree that tracks every file read, write, and creation action performed by the AI coding agent during active sessions.


## What Claude Files Pane Does


Claude Files Pane integrates directly into the Claude Code interface as a browser extension. The tool monitors the AI agent's workspace activity and renders a dynamic file tree view that updates in real time as Claude Code navigates, reads, or modifies files. When the agent opens a configuration file, edits a function, or creates a new module, the corresponding file appears highlighted in the tree structure immediately.


The extension provides three visual states for each file: unmodified (read-only access), modified (edited by the agent), and newly created. Color coding and icons distinguish these states, giving developers instant feedback on which parts of their codebase the AI has touched. The file tree mirrors the actual project directory structure, making it easy to locate specific changes within nested folder hierarchies.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 1, 2026, Claude Files Pane is available as an open-source project on GitHub. Developers can install the extension directly from the repository and begin using it with existing Claude Code sessions. The tool requires no server-side setup and runs entirely within the browser, parsing Claude Code's output stream to extract file operation data.


## Why Developers Want File Transparency


AI coding agents like Claude Code often touch dozens of files during complex refactoring tasks or multi-file feature implementations. Without visibility into these operations, developers must manually review conversation logs or rely on version control diffs after the fact. Claude Files Pane solves this friction by surfacing file activity as it happens, letting users verify that the agent is working within intended boundaries.


The tool also aids debugging. When Claude Code produces unexpected results, the file tree reveals whether the agent read outdated dependencies, skipped critical configuration files, or edited unrelated modules. This transparency helps users diagnose agent behavior and provide more precise follow-up instructions.


- Real-time tracking of file reads, writes, and creations
- Visual file tree mirroring project directory structure
- Color-coded status indicators for modified and new files
- Zero-setup browser extension with no backend dependencies


## Integration with Claude Code Workflows


Claude Files Pane complements existing Claude Code usage patterns without requiring workflow changes. The extension runs passively alongside the coding interface, automatically detecting when a session begins and populating the file tree as the agent works. Users can collapse or expand directory branches to focus on specific subsections of large projects.


For teams using Claude Code in shared repositories, the file tree view helps reviewers understand which components the AI modified during pair-programming sessions. The visualization makes it faster to spot potential conflicts before committing agent-generated changes to version control.


## What This Means


Claude Files Pane addresses a core visibility gap in AI-assisted coding. As AI agents gain autonomy over larger codebases, developers need real-time oversight tools that reveal what the agent is doing and where. This extension provides that transparency layer in an accessible, open-source package. By showing live file operations in a familiar tree interface, Claude Files Pane lowers the cognitive load of supervising AI coding agents and makes it easier to trust their output. Expect similar monitoring tools to emerge for other AI coding platforms as the community prioritizes agent observability.
